issues.problem: The URL now redirects to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/data-guide/technology-choices/understand-data-store-models. The page title is 'Understand data models', not 'Overview of data store models'. The excerpt does support the claims it is cited for: polyglot persistence, selecting models by access pattern, 'Combine models only where access patterns or life cycles clearly diverge', and search (Azure AI Search), key-value (Azure Managed Redis) and document (Cosmos DB) stores. The name 'Azure AI Search' is confirmed on the page.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the URL with the canonical redirect target. Optionally retitle the link 'Understand data models' / 'Модели данных в Azure' in both locales.

issues.claim: Ask two questions: which concrete query the primary database cannot serve at the required cost, and what happens to the data in the new store when the primary changes, fails or is restored from a backup.
issues.problem: The hint nearly restates the answer hinge: justification by an access pattern the primary cannot serve at the required cost, plus the synchronization and recovery cost. It nudges strongly toward the answer and gives away part of it. The RU hint has the same strength.
issues.suggestedFix: Make it vaguer, e.g. 'What exactly do you gain from the second store, and what must stay true about the data when the primary database changes or is restored?' Mirror the change in RU.

issues.claim: every store is one more technology to learn, run, secure and keep consistent with the others.
issues.problem: The sentence follows 'as Martin Fowler describes it'. Fowler's bliki covers only the extra interface to learn, the performance understanding needed, and the new consistency and availability questions. The run, secure, backup and operations costs are the author's own judgment, not from the cited source. The sentence does not claim otherwise, but the attribution could be read as covering them.
issues.suggestedFix: Separate the attribution from the author's own additions, e.g. 'Fowler stresses the complexity cost: a new interface to learn and new consistency questions. In practice it also means operations, backup and security.' Mirror in RU.
